text:
Marina: Drafting a compact customer-facing runbook for Day0–7 onboarding and short surges when customers use streaming + bursty batching. Goal: reduce renewal risk by keeping latency predictable. PTAL.

Marina: Quick checklist (customer copy):
- Set a short batch window for chat-heavy flows: 10–50ms for interactive; 150–300ms for throughputy background jobs.
- Add a tenant cache key header: `x-rd-cache-key: tenant:<id>:prompt-prefix` and use prefix hashing for shared prompts.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated contexts (session-level) and set cache TTL = conversation context lifespan (default 24h).
- Streaming keepalive: send a lightweight heartbeat every 10s if client holds long open streams to keep routing warm.
- Fallback model policy: if p95 latency > 1.2s for 3 consecutive minutes, route to a lower-cost variant with identical behavior.

Marina: Example curl to set cache key + small batch window:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "x-rd-cache-key: tenant:12345:welcome-flow" \
  -H "x-rd-batch-wait-ms: 30" \
  -d '{"input":"Hello"}'
```

Ben C: LGTM. One suggestion: call out concrete thresholds for renewal signal. e.g., tag account as "latency-risk" if p95 increases by >20% week-over-week AND error-rate goes up >1%.

Ben C: Also add recommended batching params for mobile apps: `x-rd-batch-size: 8` + `x-rd-batch-wait-ms: 40`.

Sylvie: Add a short escalation script for CSMs:
- Check tenant dashboard p50/p95 last 24h.
- If degraded, run quick repro with `x-rd-cache-key` toggled off to verify caching impact.
- If perf improves >30% with cache disabled, schedule ops ticket for cache invalidation strategy.

OpsBot: runbook draft saved to /kb/cs/runbooks/streaming-batch-compact-1735321000.md

Nate: From infra: include a sample query for Observability (PromQL-like):
```
avg_over_time(latency_p95{tenant="12345"}[1h])
```
And a note: prefer measuring tail latency on streaming frames, not just final token.

Alexa: For customer feedback capture, add a 1-question post-onboard microform: "Was response speed acceptable? (yes/no) + optional 20-char note". Link: https://tiny.redwood/quick-feedback

Marina: Thanks all — I'll fold these in and publish a customer-ready one-pager. @Ben C can you sign off when you have 10m? If yes I'll add to the CS playbook library and surface in enablement calls.

Ben C: Happy to sign off after small wording tweak on the fallback note. :thumbsup:

Marina: Great — merging now. Will ping when published.
